sentences.en: Let the consequences be what they may, whether the Potomac is crimsoned in human gore and Pennsylvania Avenue is paved ten fathoms deep with mangled bodies,
sentences.zh: 无论后果如何，无论波托马克河是否被人类的鲜血染红，无论宾夕法尼亚大道是否被深达十英寻的残肢断臂所铺满，

sentences.en: or whether the last vestige of liberty is swept from the face of the American continent,
sentences.zh: 无论自由的最后一点痕迹是否从美洲大陆的表面被抹去，

sentences.en: the South will never submit to such humiliation and degradation as the inauguration of Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 南方永远不会屈服于亚伯拉罕·林肯就职典礼所带来的那种羞辱和堕落。

sentences.en: Gosh, it's chilling, it's chilling.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这真令人不寒而栗，真令人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: That superb American accent.
sentences.zh: 那地道的美国口音。

sentences.en: I mean, I didn't even try and do an Atlanta accent there, but that was written.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我刚才甚至没试着模仿亚特兰大口音，但那是写在稿子里的。

sentences.en: Have you been to Georgia?
sentences.zh: 你去过佐治亚州吗？

sentences.en: I'll come to that in a minute.
sentences.zh: 我一会儿再说这个。

sentences.en: That was from the Atlanta newspaper, the Southern Confederacy in August 1860.
sentences.zh: 那是1860年8月亚特兰大报纸《南方邦联》上的内容。

sentences.en: I have been to Savannah.
sentences.zh: 我去过萨凡纳。

sentences.en: Oh, that's very Georgia.
sentences.zh: 哦，那非常有佐治亚特色。

sentences.en: I've been to Savannah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我去过萨凡纳，是的。

sentences.en: So yes, I have.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我去过。

sentences.en: But you clearly didn't pick up the local dialect.
sentences.zh: 但你显然没学会当地的方言。

sentences.en: No, I didn't, I'm afraid.
sentences.zh: 不，恐怕我没学会。

sentences.en: So many apologies to all Americans from the South who may be listening to this.
sentences.zh: 向所有可能正在收听节目的南方美国人深表歉意。

sentences.en: I put my hands up.
sentences.zh: 我举手投降。

sentences.en: I can't do it.
sentences.zh: 我学不来。

sentences.en: I really apologize.
sentences.zh: 我真的很抱歉。

sentences.en: But it's, we wanted to read that because, I mean, it is a, I mean, it's a kind of the death knell for the,
sentences.zh: 但我们之所以想读这段，是因为，我的意思是，这是一种……这算是某种丧钟，为了……

sentences.en: the peace that it held and the sense of kind of the carnage that is to come.
sentences.zh: 为了它所维持的和平，以及对即将到来的大屠杀的预感。

sentences.en: And it's a perfect introduction to part two of the episode we're doing here on the rest of history on the American Civil War.
sentences.zh: 这是我们正在做的关于美国内战历史系列节目第二部分的完美开场。

sentences.en: And in the first part, Adam Smith, great scholar of the period, took us through the causes of the war.
sentences.zh: 在第一部分中，该时期的伟大研究者亚当·史密斯带我们梳理了战争的起因。

sentences.en: And Adam, you took us up to the firing on Fort Sumter and the establishment of the Confederacy with its capital at Richmond.
sentences.zh: 亚当，你带我们了解到了萨姆特堡的炮火，以及以里士满为首都的邦联的建立。

sentences.en: At what point do you think it becomes absolutely clear that there is no way back?
sentences.zh: 你认为在哪个节点，彻底没有回头路变得显而易见？

sentences.en: Is it the firing on Fort Sumter?
sentences.zh: 是萨姆特堡的炮火吗？

sentences.en: That's what's traditionally said, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 传统说法是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: Or even after that, might it have been possible to pull back the dogs of war?
sentences.zh: 还是说即便在那之后，仍有可能收回战争的恶犬？

sentences.en: No, I don't, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 不，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: Because by that point, the, this new Confederacy had a huge burst of self-confidence.
sentences.zh: 因为到了那个节点，这个新生的邦联有着巨大的自信心爆发。

sentences.en: You know, they, they pulled it off.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们……他们成功了。

sentences.en: They pulled off what seemed to be, what may seem to us to be the most extraordinary thing to create a, a new slaveholding republic in the middle of the 19th century,
sentences.zh: 他们做到了在19世纪中叶建立一个全新的蓄奴共和国，这在我们看来似乎是最不可思议的事情，

sentences.en: but they'd done it.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: And what were the chances that the United States with virtually no standing army and what army it had was kind of strung out policing the frontier Native Americans?
sentences.zh: 而美国几乎没有常备军，仅有的军队也分散在边境地区监视美洲原住民，他们有什么胜算？

sentences.en: What, what chance had they got of subduing militarily an area that's the size of Western Europe?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么机会在军事上征服一个面积相当于西欧的地区？

sentences.en: Who, how are they going to manage that?
sentences.zh: 谁……他们打算怎么做到这一点？

sentences.en: So do they think that there simply won't be a war, that people in the North will just accept it?
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为根本不会发生战争，北方人会直接接受吗？

sentences.en: I think there's definitely many Southernists who hope that because they have a pretty low opinion of Northernists.
sentences.zh: 我认为肯定有很多南方人希望如此，因为他们对北方人的评价相当低。

sentences.en: They hope it, but do they think it?
sentences.zh: 他们希望如此，但他们真的这么认为吗？

sentences.en: I think some of them who thought it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想其中一些人是这么想的，是的。

sentences.en: Some of them calculated that the North was too divided, that it was made up of this polyglot.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人计算出北方过于分裂，是由这种混杂的人群组成的。

sentences.en: We didn't, we didn't talk in the last episode about immigration, but that's part of the, it's actually part of the story here.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集没谈到移民问题，但那其实是故事的一部分。

sentences.en: This big scale immigration of Catholic Irish into, mainly into New York and, and, and Boston, Philadelphia in the, in the 1850s.
sentences.zh: 19世纪50年代，大量天主教爱尔兰人移民到纽约、波士顿和费城。

sentences.en: And Southerners look at this and the Germans come in as well.
sentences.zh: 南方人看着这些，还有德国人也来了。

sentences.en: And the, the Southerners look at this and they think, you know, this, this polyglot conglomeration of greasy mechanics, you know, they don't know how to handle a gun.
sentences.zh: 南方人看着这些，他们心想，你知道，这群由油腻的机械工组成的混杂群体，他们根本不知道怎么用枪。

sentences.en: They've got, they've got no clue.
sentences.zh: 他们根本一窍不通。

sentences.en: They've got no capacity and there's no political will.
sentences.zh: 他们没有能力，也没有政治意愿。

sentences.en: So they're not going to be able to fight us.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不可能打败我们。

sentences.en: And, but if there is a war, there'll be one great climactic Napoleonic style battle and clearly we'll win it and it'll be job done.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果真的发生战争，只会有一场伟大的、决定性的拿破仑式战役，显然我们会赢，然后就大功告成了。

sentences.en: But Adam, I, I mean, the question that always has been on my mind is why, and I, I mean, a lot of Americans will say, oh, it's obvious, but I would say to an outsider,
sentences.zh: 但是亚当，我的意思是，一直在我脑海里的问题是为什么，很多美国人会说，哦，这很明显，但对于局外人，

sentences.en: to a non-American, it's not obvious.
sentences.zh: 对于非美国人来说，这并不明显。

sentences.en: Why do the Northerners hate slavery?
sentences.zh: 为什么北方人憎恨奴隶制？

sentences.en: They think slavery is corrupting.
sentences.zh: 他们认为奴隶制具有腐蚀性。

sentences.en: They think the South is, is, is, is sunk in sin, is, is steeped in sin.
sentences.zh: 他们认为南方沉沦在罪恶之中，浸淫在罪恶之中。

sentences.en: Why don't the Northerners just let the South go?
sentences.zh: 为什么北方人不干脆让南方离开？

sentences.en: I mean, why don't they just say, okay, sod you, set up your tin pot confederacy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么他们不直接说，好吧，去你的，去建立你们那个破烂邦联吧。

sentences.en: We've got, you know, billions more factories than you.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的工厂比你们多几十亿个。

sentences.en: We're much more prosperous.
sentences.zh: 我们繁荣得多。

sentences.en: We're much more productive.
sentences.zh: 我们生产力高得多。

sentences.en: We're not corrupted by slavery.
sentences.zh: 我们没有被奴隶制腐蚀。

sentences.en: You'll sink like a stone.
sentences.zh: 你们会像石头一样沉下去。

sentences.en: And then you'll come begging to us in 10 years, please, can we come back into the union?
sentences.zh: 然后10年后你们会回来求我们，求求你们，我们能回到联邦吗？

sentences.en: I mean, why don't, why don't, why don't they do that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么他们不这样做？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, it's a question I've been asking for 20 years, actually, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 其实，多米尼克，这个问题我也问了20年了。

sentences.en: I mean, I, I think you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: It is the, it is the question, because I think the other side of it, which is not hard for me to explain why Southerners wanted to secede.
sentences.zh: 这确实是核心问题，因为我觉得另一面，即解释南方人为何想要分裂，对我来说并不难。

sentences.en: There's a lot, there's a lot, much more being written about that question.
sentences.zh: 关于那个问题已经写了很多很多东西了。

sentences.en: And to me, it's not really a mystery at all.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那根本不是什么谜团。

sentences.en: I think they're absolutely, given their own, given the situation they were in by 1860, I think they were quite right to roll the dice.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们绝对是，考虑到他们到1860年所处的境地，我认为他们孤注一掷是完全正确的。

sentences.en: The Southerners.
sentences.zh: 南方人。

sentences.en: The Southerners, yeah.
sentences.zh: 南方人，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it turned out really, really badly for them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，结果对他们来说真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: But I think I can totally see why, given the election of Lincoln, there were going to be, there were going to be a lot more Republican presidents, potentially, where he came from,
sentences.zh: 但我完全能理解为什么在林肯当选后，可能会有更多的共和党总统，考虑到他的出身，

sentences.en: given the shifting demographics, given the electoral system.
sentences.zh: 考虑到人口结构的变化，考虑到选举制度。

sentences.en: And it's really hard to maintain an oppressive system of human enslavement.
sentences.zh: 而且维持一种压迫性的人类奴役制度真的很难。

sentences.en: You've got to know that the polity that you are existing in respects and is going to uphold the idea of property in human beings.
sentences.zh: 你必须知道你所处的政体尊重并会维护人类财产的观念。

sentences.en: And if you've got a president of the, of your country who doesn't believe that property in human beings is legitimate, that's really, really bad.
sentences.zh: 如果你的国家总统不认为人类财产是合法的，那真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: So, you know, it makes, it makes complete sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，这完全讲得通。

sentences.en: Now, there are lots of reasons why, but yeah, but hang on, the enslaved people can still escape across the North and then you won't have the Fugitive Slave Act to, to,
sentences.zh: 当然，原因有很多，但是等等，被奴役的人仍然可以逃往北方，然后你就没有《逃奴法》来，来，

sentences.en: to get your property as you think of it returned.
sentences.zh: 来追回你所认为的财产了。

sentences.en: But then they're saying, well, that wasn't working anyway.
sentences.zh: 但他们会说，反正那也没用。

sentences.en: So what have you lost, really?
sentences.zh: 所以你到底失去了什么？

sentences.en: So it makes complete sense why Southerners wanted to secede.
sentences.zh: 所以南方人想要分裂是完全讲得通的。

sentences.en: But your question, why then did Nordners respond to secession with a war to save the Union is a right one.
sentences.zh: 但你的问题，为什么北方人要以战争来回应分裂以拯救联邦，这是一个正确的问题。

sentences.en: After all, I mean, what would we do if, when Scotland votes for independence?
sentences.zh: 毕竟，如果苏格兰投票支持独立，我们会怎么做？

sentences.en: Are you going to join up to fight for the Union?
sentences.zh: 你会加入战斗去维护联邦吗？

sentences.en: Perhaps you will, Tom.
sentences.zh: 也许你会，汤姆。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I think you've written quite passionately on this.
sentences.zh: 我想你在这方面写得相当动情。

sentences.en: Tom has, Tom has got, I mean, I've been to Tom's house.
sentences.zh: 汤姆有，汤姆有……我的意思是，我去过汤姆家。

sentences.en: He's got a whole room full of stuff, like ready to go.
sentences.zh: 他有一个房间装满了东西，随时准备出发。

sentences.en: He's got like disguiseries.
sentences.zh: 他有伪装装备之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's got it all.
sentences.zh: 是的，他什么都有。

sentences.en: Well, actually, actually, we've, we've, we've, we've got a house on the North Bank of the Tweed just inside Scotland.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实，其实我们在特威德河的北岸，就在苏格兰境内有一所房子。

sentences.en: So it'll be a bridgehead.
sentences.zh: 所以那将是一个桥头堡。

sentences.en: Fort Sumter.
sentences.zh: 萨姆特堡。

sentences.en: But yeah, I mean, obviously there's your example, Adam, right?
sentences.zh: 但是的，显然有你的例子，亚当，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, here's, okay.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里是，好吧。

sentences.en: So, but anyway, I've not answered your question here.
sentences.zh: 所以，总之，我还没回答你的问题。

sentences.en: Let me try and answer your question.
sentences.zh: 让我试着回答你的问题。

sentences.en: Why, why did, I mean, the word, I mean, some people did say that, let the, let the erring sisters depart in peace.
sentences.zh: 为什么，为什么……有些人确实说过，让那些犯错的姐妹们和平离开吧。

sentences.en: It was a headline in the New York Tribune.
sentences.zh: 那是《纽约论坛报》的头条。

sentences.en: I mean, there was that, there was that sentiment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实有那种情绪。

sentences.en: But why not?
sentences.zh: 但为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Because in the end, the point is this, the United States is the last best hope of earth.
sentences.zh: 因为归根结底，重点是：美国是地球上最后的最佳希望。

sentences.en: That's Abraham Lincoln's phrase.
sentences.zh: 那是亚伯拉罕·林肯的名言。

sentences.en: It is, and just think about that.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，想想看。

sentences.en: This is the last refuge for humanity.
sentences.zh: 这是人类最后的避难所。

sentences.en: If the experiment in democracy of constitutional government is seen to fail.
sentences.zh: 如果宪政民主的实验被视为失败。

sentences.en: If the response to a duly constituted election is that half of the country or almost half of the country throws its toys out of the pram and walks out,
sentences.zh: 如果对一场正式选举的回应是，半个国家或几乎半个国家闹脾气并退出，

sentences.en: then the light of freedom will dim around the world.
sentences.zh: 那么自由之光将在世界各地黯淡。

sentences.en: But also a house divided against itself cannot stand.
sentences.zh: 而且，一个分裂的家庭是站不住脚的。

sentences.en: So, so if half the house goes and there's a risk, the whole house may collapse.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果半个房子倒塌了，整个房子也有可能倒塌。

sentences.en: So that's Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 这就是林肯的观点。

sentences.en: Lincoln made that speech, shouldn't he?
sentences.zh: 林肯发表过那个演讲，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think in the Lincoln Douglas debates that a house divided itself can't stand.
sentences.zh: 我想是在林肯-道格拉斯辩论中提到的，一个分裂的家庭站不住脚。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Isn't it?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: But I mean, if the house so patently is divided, why not just cut off the bit that's the problem, the rotten bits, as it were, and the rest of your house is going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，如果房子明显分裂了，为什么不直接切掉有问题的部分，那些腐烂的部分，剩下的房子就会很好。

sentences.en: I mean, that would be my argument.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那会是我的论点。

sentences.en: In some ways, if you're a northerner, you might well say, listen, we're a lot better off without those clowns.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，如果你是北方人，你很可能会说，听着，没有那些小丑我们会过得更好。

sentences.en: They're bad people.
sentences.zh: 他们是坏人。

sentences.en: They've got slaves.
sentences.zh: 他们有奴隶。

sentences.en: You know, they're backward.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们很落后。

sentences.en: Because that's what a lot of northerners thought about the South, right?
sentences.zh: 因为很多北方人就是这么看南方的，对吧？

sentences.en: They thought they were backward and kind of fly-bitten and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们认为他们落后，而且像被苍蝇叮咬一样，诸如此类。

sentences.en: I mean, I would say it still is quite baffling that you're prepared to lose, you know, lose, what is it,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我仍然觉得很费解，你竟然准备失去，你知道，失去，是多少，

sentences.en: more than 300,000 northerners die in the Civil War to force these people to be back in their country.
sentences.zh: 超过30万北方人在内战中死亡，只为了强迫这些人回到他们的国家。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: And you've got, I mean, I agree.
sentences.zh: 而且你有，我的意思是，我同意。

sentences.en: I think it is baffling.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实令人费解。

sentences.en: It's something I've really, I've been struggling with for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 这是我20年来一直纠结的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, you have American listeners, they can write in and tell you why us three Brits asking this question, what we're missing,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你们有美国听众，他们可以写信告诉你们为什么我们三个英国人问这个问题，我们错过了什么，

sentences.en: and why it's all so ludicrous that we're even asking the question.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么我们问这个问题本身就如此荒谬。

sentences.en: But the answer must have something to do with the idea of the Union and what it represents.
sentences.zh: 但答案一定与联邦的理念及其所代表的意义有关。

sentences.en: Yeah, it must do.
sentences.zh: 是的，一定有关。

sentences.en: And what that promise of the revolution and the Declaration of Independence represents.
sentences.zh: 以及革命和《独立宣言》所代表的承诺。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of very on brand now to sneer at the idea that there was a kind of moral imperative behind the Union in the Civil War, that it's couched in overtly cynical terMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在嘲笑内战中联邦背后存在某种道德使命的想法非常流行，这被归结为极其愤世嫉俗的术语。

sentences.en: And yet, I can't understand why they would have done it unless a certain sense of kind of an identification of their cause with what was best, not just for the North,
sentences.zh: 然而，我无法理解他们为什么要这样做，除非他们将自己的事业与不仅对北方，

sentences.en: but for the United States and for the whole of the world was in play.
sentences.zh: 而且对美国乃至全世界最有利的事物联系在一起。

sentences.en: Yes, you've put that very well.
sentences.zh: 是的，你表达得非常好。

sentences.en: That's exactly what they said repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 这正是他们反复说的。

sentences.en: And I think that's exactly what they thought.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这正是他们所想的。

sentences.en: I mean, the flip side of that was the humiliation they said they felt, how diminished they felt on the world stage as a result of secession,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其反面是他们所说的感受到的羞辱，因分裂而在世界舞台上感到多么渺小，

sentences.en: that this was a necessary project in order, the fiery trial through which they now had to pass, was necessary in order to prove themselves as a real nation on the global stage.
sentences.zh: 这是一个必要的工程，他们现在必须经历的严酷考验，对于证明他们作为全球舞台上一个真正的国家是必要的。

sentences.en: Adam, we've been talking about it so far as though North and South are absolutely distinguishable or as though, in effect, they have become two separate countries.
sentences.zh: 亚当，我们目前谈论它的方式，好像北方和南方是完全可以区分的，或者好像实际上它们已经变成了两个独立的国家。

sentences.en: But of course, we call it the American Civil War.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们称之为美国内战。

sentences.en: And that implies, you know, institutions and even families being divided.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，你知道，机构甚至家庭都被分裂了。

sentences.en: And I suppose an obvious institution that does end up divided would be West Point, which is the great U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想一个最终被分裂的明显机构就是西点军校，它是伟大的美国。

sentences.en: military academy, where large numbers of graduates and officers, commanding heights of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 军事学院，那里有大量的毕业生和军官，占据着美国的制高点，

sentences.en: Army, have to decide which of the two sides they're going to go for.
sentences.zh: 陆军，他们必须决定站在哪一边。

sentences.en: And I suppose the emblematic figure who has to make his mind up is perhaps the most famous general of all, perhaps from Ulysses S.
sentences.zh: 我想，那个必须做出决定的标志性人物，或许是所有将军中最著名的一位，可能仅次于尤利西斯·S·

sentences.en: Grant, which is the guy who ends up leading the Confederacy, Robert E.
sentences.zh: 格兰特，而这个人最终领导了邦联，他就是罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee.
sentences.zh: 李。

sentences.en: So what's his background?
sentences.zh: 那么他的背景是什么？

sentences.en: How does he and how does he come to choose the Confederacy over the Union?
sentences.zh: 他是如何以及为什么最终选择支持邦联而不是联邦的？

sentences.en: Because he actually gets offered the leadership of the Union, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为他实际上被邀请担任联邦的领导人，不是吗？

sentences.en: He does, because he's regarded as one of the most able officers in the United States Army in 1860, 1861.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，因为在1860年、1861年，他被认为是美国陆军中最有能力的军官之一。

sentences.en: He is a career army officer, but he's a Virginian.
sentences.zh: 他是一名职业陆军军官，但他是个弗吉尼亚人。

sentences.en: We mentioned him in the last episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集提到过他。

sentences.en: He was the guy who arrested John Brown when Brown launched his raid on Harper's Ferry in Virginia
sentences.zh: 当约翰·布朗在弗吉尼亚州的哈珀斯费里发动突袭时，正是他逮捕了布朗，

sentences.en: to trying to distribute the guns from that arsenal and set off a slave insurrection.
sentences.zh: 试图分发那个军火库里的枪支并引发奴隶起义。

sentences.en: So, you know, the story about Lee that has been told down the generations and that is much cherished by, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，关于李的故事在几代人中流传，并且被，你知道，

sentences.en: has been much cherished, still is, by white Southerners is that he was in an agony of indecision.
sentences.zh: 一直被白人南方人所珍视，至今依然如此，那就是他当时处于极度的犹豫不决之中。

sentences.en: You know, what should he do?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他该怎么办？

sentences.en: You know, he's after all, he's an officer of the United States.
sentences.zh: 你知道，毕竟他是一名美国军官。

sentences.en: So he's sworn an oath to uphold the Constitution of the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以他宣誓要维护美国宪法。

sentences.en: But in his heart, he's a Virginian and he's completely divided on what's he going to do.
sentences.zh: 但在内心深处，他是个弗吉尼亚人，对于该怎么做，他完全处于分裂状态。

sentences.en: In the end, he can't bring himself to lead an army of invasion into his home state.
sentences.zh: 最终，他无法让自己去领导一支入侵自己家乡的军队。

sentences.en: That's the story that's told about Roddy Lee.
sentences.zh: 这就是关于罗伯特·李的故事。

sentences.en: Well, I think that is giving, I think what that undersells is the extent to which Lee, he, like other elite white Virginians, was fundamentally committed to slavery.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这种说法，我认为它低估了李在多大程度上，像其他弗吉尼亚白人精英一样，从根本上致力于维护奴隶制。

sentences.en: Well, because his wife owns large numbers of plantations, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为他的妻子拥有大量的种植园，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And slaves.
sentences.zh: 还有奴隶。

sentences.en: And yes, he's fully married into, he's part of a Virginia dynasty that has owned slaves for generations.
sentences.zh: 是的，他完全融入了那个家族，他是弗吉尼亚王朝的一部分，这个王朝几代人都拥有奴隶。

sentences.en: He cannot, he temperamentally, culturally, intellectually, politically, he is, he loathes everything that this new insurgent, radical Republican,
sentences.zh: 他不能，从气质、文化、知识、政治上讲，他厌恶这个新的、叛乱的、激进的共和党所代表的一切，

sentences.en: as he would, as his, people would probably call it like him, the Black Republican Party represents.
sentences.zh: 正如他，正如他的人可能称呼的那样，像他一样，称之为“黑人共和党”。

sentences.en: He's just no way, no way that Robert E.
sentences.zh: 他根本不可能，罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee is ever going, was ever going to be comfortable leading the Union army.
sentences.zh: 李绝不可能，也绝不会愿意去领导联邦军队。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because it's an important part of his brand that he's, so he gets compared to a perfect British gentleman by, you know, British observer during the war.
sentences.zh: 因为这是他个人品牌的重要组成部分，所以他被战争期间的英国观察家比作完美的英国绅士，你知道。

sentences.en: He's a kind of silver fox.
sentences.zh: 他是一种“银狐”。

sentences.en: He's very stylish.
sentences.zh: 他非常有风度。

sentences.en: Well, that's the Confederacy's brand though, Tom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但那是邦联的品牌，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, that really is the Confederacy's brand.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那确实是邦联的品牌。

sentences.en: I mean, I read, in my children's history book, that I read in the 1970s, that was the Confederacy's brand.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我在我20世纪70年代读的孩子们的历史书里读到过，那就是邦联的品牌。

sentences.en: And so that's why, that could have Cavaliers.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么，那可能拥有骑士精神。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that is why Lee is the kind of, I mean, he's in a sense, the Prince Rupert of, of the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么李是那种，我的意思是，他在某种意义上是邦联的鲁珀特亲王。

sentences.en: He's the dashing Cavalier.
sentences.zh: 他是潇洒的骑士。

sentences.en: He's the emblem of it.
sentences.zh: 他是它的象征。

sentences.en: But in essence, he is doing it because he wants to keep his children's inheritance safe.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，他这样做是因为他想保护他孩子们的遗产。

sentences.en: And that inheritance consists of plantations and of human property.
sentences.zh: 而那份遗产包括种植园和人类财产。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the vision of America that he understands and that he understands he's inherited from his ancestors who fought in the revolution is one that fundamentally includes slavery.
sentences.zh: 他所理解的美国愿景，以及他认为从参加革命的祖先那里继承来的愿景，从根本上是包含奴隶制的。

sentences.en: And as it were, what, you know, why shouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Because that's what the Republic has always done.
sentences.zh: 因为共和国一直以来都是这样做的。

sentences.en: And so he's standing against revolution, as he sees it.
sentences.zh: 所以在他看来，他是在反抗革命。

sentences.en: I mean, he could not conceive that a United States run by these new Republicans was going to be one that he would recognize.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他无法想象一个由这些新共和党人管理的美国会是他所能认同的。

sentences.en: His world is about to end if the Republicans' vision for America dominates.
sentences.zh: 如果共和党人对美国的愿景占据主导地位，他的世界即将终结。

sentences.en: And let's sort of pull back the camera back a bit.
sentences.zh: 让我们把镜头拉远一点。

sentences.en: So by the summer of 1861, you have, I think, 11 states in the Confederate States of America.
sentences.zh: 到1861年夏天，我想，美利坚联盟国有11个州。

sentences.en: They've got a population of 9 million people.
sentences.zh: 他们有900万人口。

sentences.en: Three and a half million of them or so are slaves.
sentences.zh: 其中大约350万是奴隶。

sentences.en: And they are against 22 states in the Union.
sentences.zh: 他们对抗的是联邦的22个州。

sentences.en: So the Rump Union, if you like, R-USA, I suppose you would call them, with 22 million people, but massive advantages in mills, factories, railroads and all those things.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你愿意的话，剩下的联邦，我想你可以称之为“R-USA”，有2200万人口，但在工厂、铁路和所有这些方面都有巨大的优势。

sentences.en: We know now, everybody listening to this knows that the Union wins.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，听这个节目的每个人都知道联邦赢了。

sentences.en: Just to go through those facts and figures, it makes it sound like, okay, it's just like playing out a board game.
sentences.zh: 仅仅回顾这些事实和数据，听起来就像，好吧，这就像在玩棋盘游戏。

sentences.en: You know you've got all the cards.
sentences.zh: 你知道你手里有所有的牌。

sentences.en: We've got two questions which go together well.
sentences.zh: 我们有两个可以很好地结合在一起的问题。

sentences.en: One is, Grant Rogers, why did the Union Army lose so many battles at first?
sentences.zh: 一个是格兰特·罗杰斯的：为什么联邦军队起初输掉了那么多战斗？

sentences.en: Spoiler alert, they do.
sentences.zh: 剧透预警，他们确实输了。

sentences.en: And Will Randall, did the South stand a chance and was the North always going to win?
sentences.zh: 另一个是威尔·兰德尔的：南方有机会吗？北方是否注定会赢？

sentences.en: So I think those questions kind of go together, really, because it's the fact that the North doesn't win a kind of crushing victory initially that allows the war to go on,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这些问题确实是相关的，因为正是北方最初没有取得那种压倒性的胜利，才使得战争得以持续，

sentences.en: but sets up the question of was the North always going to win?
sentences.zh: 但也引出了“北方是否注定会赢”这个问题。

sentences.en: I think the North was always going to win if it could stay the course.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果北方能坚持到底，它注定会赢。

sentences.en: If the war went on long enough for it to bring to bear its advantages in men and material and its diplomatic advantages and its territorial advantages and everything else,
sentences.zh: 如果战争持续的时间足够长，让它能够发挥其在人力、物力、外交、领土以及其他各方面的优势，

sentences.en: if the war went on long enough.
sentences.zh: 如果战争持续得足够长的话。

sentences.en: But it might not have done.
sentences.zh: 但它可能不会那样。

sentences.en: It might have ended earlier than that.
sentences.zh: 它可能在那之前就结束了。

sentences.en: So there are scenarios, I think, which we can talk about.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有一些我们可以讨论的情景。

sentences.en: We can imagine scenarios short of the total military victory that the North, in the end, won.
sentences.zh: 我们可以想象出一些不同于北方最终取得全面军事胜利的情景。

sentences.en: I mean, isn't that the only way they win, though, Adam, with the total military victory?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，亚当，难道这不是他们获胜的唯一方式吗，通过全面的军事胜利？

sentences.en: Because all the Confederacy has to do is just somehow plot along and keep going, and they'll eventually win, right?
sentences.zh: 因为邦联所要做的只是设法拖延并坚持下去，他们最终就会赢，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the North will settle and then...
sentences.zh: 因为北方会妥协，然后……

sentences.en: So the Confederate objectives are to persuade the North that this isn't a war, that they can win in that total way, that it isn't worth the enormous coSt.
sentences.zh: 所以邦联的目标是说服北方，这不是一场他们能以那种全面方式获胜的战争，这不值得付出巨大的代价。

sentences.en: And therefore, because the United States is a democracy, albeit only with men voting and essentially white men voting, but it's subject to public opinion.
sentences.zh: 因此，因为美国是一个民主国家，尽管只有男性投票，本质上是白人男性投票，但它受公众舆论的影响。

sentences.en: And so it follows then that, logically, Confederate military strategy was focused on Northern public opinion.
sentences.zh: 所以逻辑上讲，邦联的军事战略是针对北方公众舆论的。

sentences.en: Robert E.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee got this.
sentences.zh: 李明白这一点。

sentences.en: You know, he knew that in the end, what he had to do was to persuade ordinary Northern people that this wasn't a war that was worth fighting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他知道最终他必须做的是说服普通的北方民众，这不是一场值得打的战争。

sentences.en: That's what the South had to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是南方必须做的。

sentences.en: What the North had to do, as you say, Dominic, is to completely destroy the South, which in the end was what they did.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，多米尼克，北方必须做的是彻底摧毁南方，这最终也是他们所做的。

sentences.en: But it took them four years.
sentences.zh: 但这花了他们四年时间。

sentences.en: And it took them four years to marshal their superior resources.
sentences.zh: 这花了他们四年时间来集结他们优越的资源。

sentences.en: So by the very end of the war, by the final year of the war, the North was fighting essentially a war of attrition,
sentences.zh: 所以到了战争的最后，到了战争的最后一年，北方本质上是在打一场消耗战，

sentences.en: which it was pummeling the South day after day after day after day, often losing more men than the South in any given battle.
sentences.zh: 它日复一日地猛烈打击南方，在任何一场战斗中损失的人员往往比南方还多。

sentences.en: But it could afford to do so.
sentences.zh: 但它负担得起。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Adam, one other way in which people say that the Confederacy, I mean, wouldn't have been able to hold out, perhaps, is if the European powers, and perhaps particularly Britain,
sentences.zh: 那么亚当，人们说邦联无法坚持下去的另一个原因，也许是如果欧洲列强，特别是英国，

sentences.en: had entered the war on its side.
sentences.zh: 站在它那一边参战的话。

sentences.en: And so you mentioned about the Confederacy sending emissaries to Paris and to London.
sentences.zh: 你提到了邦联派遣特使前往巴黎和伦敦。

sentences.en: What would have happened if either the French or the British had come in on the Confederate side?
sentences.zh: 如果法国或英国站在邦联一边参战，会发生什么？

sentences.en: And was there ever any prospect of that happening?
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生的可能性大吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is kind of always the sort of deus ex machina for the South, right?
sentences.zh: 这对于南方来说，总是那种“机械降神”式的希望，对吧？

sentences.en: This notion that there would be some foreign intervention.
sentences.zh: 这种认为会有某种外国干预的观念。

sentences.en: And after all, they knew how this would work, because they could look back to the American War of Independence, right?
sentences.zh: 毕竟，他们知道这会如何运作，因为他们可以回顾美国独立战争，对吧？

sentences.en: So there was a war in which a bunch of sort of scrappy colonials with no proper army defeated the world's leading military superpower.
sentences.zh: 那是一场一群没有正规军的乌合之众击败了世界领先军事超级大国的战争。

sentences.en: I mean, what were the chances of that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那样的几率有多大？

sentences.en: Well, one of the ways in which they did it, of course, was with French military help.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们成功的方式之一，当然是得到了法国的军事援助。

sentences.en: So they had a template there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有一个模板。

sentences.en: Get the French involved again, or get the Brits involved.
sentences.zh: 让法国再次介入，或者让英国介入。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, you changed the military balance.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，你就改变了军事平衡。

sentences.en: And they had, you know, they had good reason for optimism.
sentences.zh: 而且他们有充分的理由感到乐观。

sentences.en: I mean, after all, if, and it's obviously a very big if, you take slavery out of the equation, then what the Southerners were doing in 1861 is national self-determination.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，毕竟，如果——这显然是一个非常大的“如果”——你把奴隶制从等式中剔除，那么南方人在1861年所做的是民族自决。

sentences.en: If you're a British liberal, you know, if you're Gladstone, or more to the point, if you're Richard Cobden,
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个英国自由主义者，你知道，如果你是格莱斯顿，或者更确切地说，如果你是理查德·科布登，

sentences.en: you look at this and you're kind of, you know, your head explodes, because national self-determination, obviously good.
sentences.zh: 你看着这一切，你会觉得，你知道，你的头都要炸了，因为民族自决显然是好事。

sentences.en: Like, what's not to like about that?
sentences.zh: 就像，那有什么不好的？

sentences.en: The Southerners support free trade.
sentences.zh: 南方人支持自由贸易。

sentences.en: They're anti-protectionists.
sentences.zh: 他们是反保护主义者。

sentences.en: That's obviously good.
sentences.zh: 那显然是好事。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, they're slaveholders.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，他们是奴隶主。

sentences.en: That's a bit of a problem.
sentences.zh: 那是个问题。

sentences.en: So what, you know, and so British liberals were in this genuine dilemma at the start of the war.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，英国自由主义者在战争初期确实陷入了这种困境。

sentences.en: But the fact that at the beginning of the war, Lincoln and the Union said, well, this is not a war to end slavery.
sentences.zh: 但战争初期林肯和联邦说，好吧，这不是一场结束奴隶制的战争。

sentences.en: This is just a war to keep the Union together.
sentences.zh: 这只是一场为了保持联邦统一的战争。

sentences.en: It meant that there was space in British liberal radical circles to say, well, okay, if this really isn't a war to end slavery, then,
sentences.zh: 这意味着在英国自由激进派圈子里有空间说，好吧，如果这真的不是一场结束奴隶制的战争，那么，

sentences.en: and maybe, as you know, as Dominic was saying earlier, maybe actually slavery will come to an end earlier, if it's kind of quarantined in this new Confederate.
sentences.zh: 也许，正如你所知，正如多米尼克刚才所说，如果奴隶制被隔离在这个新的邦联中，也许它会更早结束。

sentences.en: And then we can apply sanctions.
sentences.zh: 然后我们可以实施制裁。

sentences.en: We can use economic influence somehow or other, potentially we can blockade them.
sentences.zh: 我们可以以某种方式利用经济影响力，潜在地我们可以封锁他们。

sentences.en: We can stop imports of new slaves.
sentences.zh: 我们可以停止进口新奴隶。

sentences.en: Maybe slavery can end more quickly.
sentences.zh: 也许奴隶制能更快结束。

sentences.en: Yeah, but also, Adam, isn't it the case that you could argue it's in Britain's strategic interest to break up the United States?
sentences.zh: 是的，但亚当，难道不能说分裂美国符合英国的战略利益吗？

sentences.en: I mean, there are fears all through the 19th century that there could be war between the United States and British North America.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个19世纪人们都担心美国和英属北美之间可能会爆发战争。

sentences.en: You know, what becomes Canada?
sentences.zh: 你知道，也就是后来的加拿大。

sentences.en: So surely, I mean, isn't there an argument from kind of Palmerston and people like that?
sentences.zh: 所以肯定，我的意思是，帕默斯顿和类似的人难道没有这种论点吗？

sentences.en: Listen, let's pile in, smash it all up.
sentences.zh: 听着，让我们加入进去，把这一切都砸碎。

sentences.en: Great for us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说太棒了。

sentences.en: We're even more top nation than we were already.
sentences.zh: 我们比以前更加处于顶尖国家的地位了。

sentences.en: The pesky colonials have been taught a lesson.
sentences.zh: 那些讨厌的殖民者得到了教训。

sentences.en: And it's pretty much what the French are doing in Mexico, right?
sentences.zh: 这和法国在墨西哥所做的事情差不多，对吧？

sentences.en: So we did an episode on the extraordinary French adventure in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 我们做过一期关于法国在墨西哥那场非凡冒险的节目。

sentences.en: And that basically is an attempt to try and set up a French zone of influence while the Americans are distracted.
sentences.zh: 那基本上是试图在美利坚人分心时建立一个法国势力范围。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Since the French are already militarily engaged in North America with this bizarre intervention in Mexico,
sentences.zh: 既然法国已经通过在墨西哥那场离奇的干预在北美进行了军事介入，

sentences.en: Napoleon III is probably more likely to come in on in support of the Confederacy in the end than Britain.
sentences.zh: 拿破仑三世最终支持邦联的可能性可能比英国更大。

sentences.en: Everything you say is totally right, Dominic, about the kind of schadenfreude and the kind of gleeful enjoyment of the of the Americans going to war with one another in 1861.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你说的一切都完全正确，关于那种幸灾乐祸，以及对1861年美国人相互开战的那种幸灾乐祸的享受。

sentences.en: One, what are the countervailing factors that meant that in the end, I actually kind of, you know, to answer your question,
sentences.zh: 第一，有什么抵消因素意味着最终，我实际上，你知道，回答你的问题，

sentences.en: was Britain ever likely to intervene on the part of the Confederacy?
sentences.zh: 英国是否真的可能站在邦联一边干预？

sentences.en: I think no is the answer.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案是否定的。

sentences.en: What were the countervailing factors?
sentences.zh: 那些抵消因素是什么？

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: one of them was the city of London and the massive amounts of investment that had been made in United States railroads and that all would have been put in jeopardy if Britain then had to go to war with the United States,
sentences.zh: 其中之一是伦敦金融城，以及在美利坚铁路上的巨额投资，如果英国不得不与美国开战，所有这些都将岌岌可危，

sentences.en: which presumably would have been the inevitable consequence of intervention in support of the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 而这大概是支持邦联进行干预的必然结果。

sentences.en: And the second one in the end was slavery.
sentences.zh: 第二个因素最终还是奴隶制。

sentences.en: In the end, as it became clearer and clearer, that union victory in the war would deal likely an irreparable blow to slavery.
sentences.zh: 最终，随着越来越清楚的是，联邦在战争中的胜利可能会给奴隶制带来不可挽回的打击，

sentences.en: It became harder and harder to imagine how a British government would do anything to actively support a pro-slavery republic.
sentences.zh: 英国政府想要采取任何行动来积极支持一个支持奴隶制的共和国，就变得越来越难以想象了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that among the liberals, as you say that, I mean, they can't do it really, can they deep down?
sentences.zh: 而且正如你所说，在自由派人士中，我的意思是，他们内心深处其实做不到，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They can't pile in to support slaveholders because although as cynical and as ruthless as lots of liberal politicians are, they are, as Tom would say, they are deeply Christian.
sentences.zh: 他们无法全力支持奴隶主，因为尽管许多自由派政客既愤世嫉俗又冷酷无情，但正如汤姆所说，他们骨子里是非常虔诚的基督徒。

sentences.en: And well, I think we should take a break at this point.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想我们现在该休息一下了。

sentences.en: When we come back, I think we should look at the actual course of the war.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我认为我们应该看看战争的实际进程。

sentences.en: So we've kind of alluded to the fact that basically it's Confederate successes all the way and effectively that establishes a stalemate.
sentences.zh: 我们之前提到过，基本上南方邦联一路高歌猛进，实际上形成了僵局。

sentences.en: I hope I've got that right.
sentences.zh: 希望我没记错。

sentences.en: Tom, am I not right in thinking for any listeners who attempted to disappear, you're also going to be talking about cricket?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，对于那些试图溜走的听众，我没记错的话，你接下来还要谈谈板球，对吧？

sentences.en: Possibly.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: But I don't want to scare any remaining American listeners.
sentences.zh: 但我不想吓跑剩下的美国听众。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: See you after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息后再见。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: We've been talking about the American Civil War.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论美国内战。

sentences.en: We've been talking about how it started, why people chose sides and why Britain did not get involved.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了它是如何开始的，人们为何选择阵营，以及英国为何没有介入。

sentences.en: Now, Adam,
sentences.zh: 现在，亚当，

sentences.en: Tom and I were discussing this before we started recording and the complexity – we are not military historians by any means – and the complexity of the sort of battle narrative,
sentences.zh: 汤姆和我在录音前讨论过这个问题，那种复杂性——我们绝非军事历史学家——以及那种战斗叙事的复杂性，

sentences.en: I think our puny minds struggle to kind of – It just explode.
sentences.zh: 我想我们那点微薄的脑力很难去……简直要爆炸了。

sentences.en: Yeah, to compute.
sentences.zh: 没错，难以消化。

sentences.en: It just explode.
sentences.zh: 简直要爆炸了。

sentences.en: So are we right in thinking that basically it's a stalemate for the first 18 months or so in which the Confederates probably win more battles than the Union?
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为在最初的18个月左右，基本上处于僵局，而南方邦联赢得的战斗可能比联邦更多，这种看法对吗？

sentences.en: Is that about right?
sentences.zh: 大概是这样吗？

sentences.en: The only problem I have with the word stalemate is that implies there isn't any movement, any territorial gains, and there is.
sentences.zh: 我对“僵局”这个词唯一的异议是，它暗示没有任何进展，没有任何领土收益，但实际上是有的。

sentences.en: So in the Western theatre, I mean, the Union makes some significant gains.
sentences.zh: 在西部战场，我的意思是，联邦取得了一些重大进展。

sentences.en: I mean, New Orleans falls to – well, the Union Navy plays a key role there in the spring of 1862.
sentences.zh: 我是说，新奥尔良陷落了——好吧，联邦海军在1862年春季在那里发挥了关键作用。

sentences.en: So much of the Mississippi Valley is under Union control.
sentences.zh: 所以密西西比河谷的大部分地区都在联邦的控制之下。

sentences.en: So I think stalemate would be an exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为用“僵局”来形容有点夸张了。

sentences.en: But if you look at the Virginia theatre, so inevitably a lot of the battles were focused on this area between the two capitals, Richmond and Washington.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看弗吉尼亚战场，不可避免地，很多战斗都集中在里士满和华盛顿这两个首都之间的区域。

sentences.en: And that was the place that was easier for news reporters to get to.
sentences.zh: 那是新闻记者最容易到达的地方。

sentences.en: So that was where Robert E.
sentences.zh: 所以那里就是罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee was in – by the spring of 1862 was put in command of Confederate forces, the Army of Northern Virginia.
sentences.zh: 李——到1862年春天被任命为南方邦联军队（北弗吉尼亚军团）的指挥官——所在的地方。

sentences.en: So that was the kind of – that was the glamour end of the war.
sentences.zh: 所以那是战争中所谓的“光鲜”前线。

sentences.en: And certainly throughout the spring and summer of 1862, it was the Confederates in the driving seat all the way.
sentences.zh: 当然，在1862年的整个春夏，南方邦联一直处于主导地位。

sentences.en: So Lee is the kind of – the poster boy.
sentences.zh: 所以李是那种……海报男孩。

sentences.en: But the other poster boy for that is Stonewall Jackson.
sentences.zh: 但另一个海报男孩是“石墙”杰克逊。

sentences.en: Tom loves Stonewall Jackson, Adam.
sentences.zh: 汤姆很喜欢“石墙”杰克逊，亚当。

sentences.en: Well, I don't love –
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不是喜欢……

sentences.en: Tom has a very soft spot.
sentences.zh: 汤姆对他情有独钟。

sentences.en: Now, I know – I don't want to get you cancelled, Tom, because having soft spots for Confederate generals is quite dodgy.
sentences.zh: 现在，我知道——我不想让你被取消资格，汤姆，因为对南方邦联将军情有独钟是很危险的。

sentences.en: But you – I know you have a torn dress for Stonewall Jackson.
sentences.zh: 但你——我知道你对“石墙”杰克逊有种特殊的迷恋。

sentences.en: Well, well, so a question from Brad Smith.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧，那么布拉德·史密斯提了一个问题。

sentences.en: How should history view figures like Robert E.
sentences.zh: 历史应该如何看待罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee and Stonewall Jackson?
sentences.zh: 李和“石墙”杰克逊这样的人物？

sentences.en: I – we'll come to that when – you know, in due course.
sentences.zh: 我——我们到时候会谈到的，你知道的，在适当的时候。

sentences.en: I think Stonewall Jackson is kind of an interesting figure, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 我觉得“石墙”杰克逊是个很有趣的人物，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's – the archetype of the kind of the Confederate general is, well, cavalier.
sentences.zh: 因为他是——南方邦联将军那种原型的化身，嗯，骑士精神。

sentences.en: Long hair.
sentences.zh: 长发。

sentences.en: Long hair, kind of dashing, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 长发，那种风度翩翩，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Stonewall Jackson is slightly made of sterner stuff.
sentences.zh: “石墙”杰克逊的构成则要严厉得多。

sentences.en: I mean, he is a more Cromwellian figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他更像是一个克伦威尔式的人物。

sentences.en: He is – you know, he teaches black children at Sunday school and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他——你知道，他在主日学校教黑人孩子读书，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And the fact that he gets the nickname, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他得到这个绰号的事实，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because in the very first battle at Bull Run, there's the threat that the Confederate line will give way.
sentences.zh: 因为在第一次布尔河战役中，南方邦联的防线面临崩溃的威胁。

sentences.en: And he stands still and he's compared to a Stonewall.
sentences.zh: 他屹立不动，被比作一堵“石墙”。

sentences.en: Am I right in seeing him as a kind of distinctive – a distinctive figure?
sentences.zh: 我把他看作一个独特的人物，对吗？

sentences.en: Or is he just part of this blur of kind of dashing, morally dubious Confederate generals?
sentences.zh: 还是说他只是那些风度翩翩、道德可疑的南方邦联将军模糊形象的一部分？

sentences.en: There is something about Stonewall Jackson, isn't there?
sentences.zh: “石墙”杰克逊身上确实有些特别之处，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, my mother-in-law, like you, is a big – is a big fan of Stonewall Jackson.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我岳母和你一样，是“石墙”杰克逊的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: I just – to go on the record, I wouldn't describe myself as a big fan.
sentences.zh: 我只是——郑重声明，我不会称自己为超级粉丝。

sentences.en: But he does seem an intriguing figure.
sentences.zh: 但他确实是一个引人入胜的人物。

sentences.en: He is an intriguing figure.
sentences.zh: 他确实是一个引人入胜的人物。

sentences.en: He sucks lemons, I believe, as he goes into battle.
sentences.zh: 我相信他在上战场时会嚼柠檬。

sentences.en: There's been a lot of talk about that, hasn't there, about whether he ate lemons or whatever.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点有很多讨论，不是吗，关于他是否吃柠檬之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: And peaches as well, I gather.
sentences.zh: 我还听说他也吃桃子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I've never quite thought about it as he complicates the cavalier roundhead divide.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我从未想过他会打破那种“骑士派”与“圆颅党”的对立。

sentences.en: But you're totally right, Tom, that he does, because he is.
sentences.zh: 但你是完全正确的，汤姆，他确实打破了，因为他就是。

sentences.en: He is a kind of roundhead figure in a cavalier army.
sentences.zh: 他是一支骑士派军队中的圆颅党式人物。

sentences.en: And maybe that's what makes him stand out among Confederate generals.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是他在南方邦联将军中脱颖而出的原因。

sentences.en: I never quite thought about it like that before, but I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未这样想过，但我认为你是对的。

sentences.en: But Adam, is it?
sentences.zh: 但是亚当，是这样吗？

sentences.en: Is it?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, so the stereotypical view – and actually, you get this right at the end of the war, the surrender at Appomattox Courthouse, Ulysses S.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那种刻板印象——实际上，你在战争结束时，在阿波马托克斯法院的投降仪式上就能看到，尤利西斯·S·

sentences.en: Grant, the Union commander, is all kind of muddy and shabby figure, and Robert E.
sentences.zh: 格兰特，联邦指挥官，看起来满身泥泞、衣衫褴褛，而罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lears in his best uniform and a nice hat and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 李穿着他最好的制服，戴着漂亮的帽子，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And that's the sort of – I mean, that's the 1970s kind of children's book version of the war.
sentences.zh: 那就是那种——我的意思是，那是20世纪70年代儿童读物版本的战争。

sentences.en: And the version that I think a lot of Americans in the 20th century grew up with.
sentences.zh: 也是我认为许多20世纪美国人成长过程中所接触的版本。

sentences.en: Is that cavalier stuff – I mean, we can get in a later episode, I think, to the lost cause of the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 那种骑士精神的东西——我的意思是，我想我们可以在以后的节目中讨论南方邦联的“迷途事业”。

sentences.en: Is that all just nonsense?
sentences.zh: 那全是胡说八道吗？

sentences.en: I mean, these are slave owners.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些人是奴隶主。

sentences.en: These are slaveholders.
sentences.zh: 他们是蓄奴者。

sentences.en: And as these people, some of them professional military men, I mean, they're not just sort of simpering, gone-with-the-wind style fops with big hair, are they?
sentences.zh: 而且这些人，其中一些是职业军人，我的意思是，他们不仅仅是那种《乱世佳人》风格、留着长发、矫揉造作的花花公子，对吧？

sentences.en: No, they're definitely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不是。

sentences.en: Whether or not it all falls depends on what you kind of want to do with this cavalier-roundhead dichotomy.
sentences.zh: 这一切是否成立，取决于你想如何运用这种“骑士派-圆颅党”的二分法。

sentences.en: Because I think culturally, religiously, temperamentally, there is, I think, some truth
sentences.zh: 因为我认为在文化、宗教和气质上，我认为这种观点是有一定道理的，

sentences.en: in the notion that this is a forlorn – this is what seems in retrospect to be a forlorn effort
sentences.zh: 即这是一种绝望的——回顾过去，这似乎是一种绝望的努力，

sentences.en: by people who are defending a kind of older system of values against a more modern army.
sentences.zh: 由那些捍卫一种旧价值观体系的人对抗一支更现代化的军队。

sentences.en: So, you know, if that's what you mean by the cavalier-roundhead division, then I think there is some truth to it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果这就是你所说的“骑士派-圆颅党”划分的意思，那么我认为它确实有一定道理。

sentences.en: But, of course, you're right that, yeah, these people are – I mean, the officer class in particular,
sentences.zh: 但当然，你是对的，是的，这些人是——我的意思是，军官阶层尤其如此，

sentences.en: anyway, in the Army of Northern Virginia are overwhelmingly slaveholders, or the sons of slaveholders.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，北弗吉尼亚军团的军官绝大多数是奴隶主，或者是奴隶主的儿子。

sentences.en: But let's talk a bit about the experience of being a soldier in the American Civil War.
sentences.zh: 但让我们谈谈美国内战中士兵的经历。

sentences.en: So the standard thing that people say – Tom said it right at the beginning of the first episode, in his beautiful Karl Marx quotation, was about it as a sort of modern –
sentences.zh: 人们常说的一件事——汤姆在第一集开头就说了，引用了卡尔·马克思那句精彩的话，关于它是一种现代——

sentences.en: it's the first modern war.
sentences.zh: 这是第一场现代战争。

sentences.en: It's a war full of novelty.
sentences.zh: 这是一场充满新奇事物的战争。

sentences.en: But that makes it a horrible war, isn't it, as a soldier?
sentences.zh: 但这让它成为了一场可怕的战争，不是吗，作为一名士兵？

sentences.en: I mean, is it too fanciful to see it as a little bit – you know, it's a lot of – it's a very First World War at times.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，把它看作一点点——你知道，有时它非常像第一次世界大战，这太离谱了吗？

sentences.en: There's an awful lot of mud.
sentences.zh: 到处都是泥泞。

sentences.en: There is – you know, you're being hit by shrapnel.
sentences.zh: 有——你知道，你会被弹片击中。

sentences.en: There's a lot of disease behind the lines.
sentences.zh: 后方有很多疾病。

sentences.en: The conditions are horrible.
sentences.zh: 条件非常恶劣。

sentences.en: What do the men themselves think of it?
sentences.zh: 士兵们自己是怎么想的？

sentences.en: It becomes more and more like the First World War.
sentences.zh: 它变得越来越像第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: So if you – if we were transported now to outside Petersburg and Virginia in August 1864, we'd see entrenchments, barbed wire, proto-machine guns.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你——如果我们现在被传送到1864年8月的弗吉尼亚州彼得斯堡外，我们会看到战壕、铁丝网、原始机枪。

sentences.en: We'd see union mining engineers tunnelling under Confederate lines in order to blow holes underneath it, in order to try to engineer in advance, just like on the Western Front.
sentences.zh: 我们会看到联邦工兵在南方邦联防线下挖掘隧道，以便在下面炸开洞口，试图推进，就像在西线战场一样。

sentences.en: But if –
sentences.zh: 但如果——

sentences.en: It's also Napoleonic, right, as well, though.
sentences.zh: 但它也带有拿破仑战争的色彩，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: Because you've got Cavalry, you've got Custer, you've got Jeb Stuart.
sentences.zh: 因为你有骑兵，你有卡斯特，你有杰布·斯图尔特。

sentences.en: And that's why it's a classic transition war.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它是一场经典的过渡战争。

sentences.en: And so certainly through most of 1861, 62, 63, you wouldn't have seen much or any of that.
sentences.zh: 所以当然在1861、62、63年的大部分时间里，你不会看到太多或任何这些东西。

sentences.en: You would have seen some entrenchments in some places, but you certainly would have seen Cavalry charges.
sentences.zh: 你在某些地方会看到一些战壕，但你肯定会看到骑兵冲锋。

sentences.en: And all through, and really right up until the end of the war, this continuing faith that bayonet charges, the kind of cult of the bayonet charge,
